description: Computer Knowledge - Networking (18.8) question bank derived from FDA/SDA comprehensive notes. Verify and expand before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a computer network?

options.A: A single computing device used for data processing
options.B: A group of two or more computing devices connected to exchange data and share resources
options.C: A software program that manages files on a computer
options.D: A type of operating system used in servers

questions.explanation: A computer network is a group of two or more computing devices connected so that they can exchange data and share resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main purpose of computer networking?

options.A: To increase the physical size of computers
options.B: To enable communication, data exchange and sharing of resources such as files, printers, applications and Internet connections
options.C: To replace operating systems with network software
options.D: To eliminate the need for storage devices

questions.explanation: The main purpose is to enable communication, data exchange and sharing of resources such as files, printers, applications and Internet connections.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a node in a network?

options.A: Only a computer that stores data
options.B: Any device or connection point that can send, receive or forward data on a network
options.C: A cable used to connect two computers
options.D: A software application installed on a server

questions.explanation: A node is any device or connection point that can send, receive or forward data on a network, such as a computer, printer, switch or router.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a link in a network?

options.A: A software protocol used for encryption
options.B: A wired or wireless connection through which data travels between network nodes
options.C: A type of IP address assigned to a router
options.D: A database that stores network user credentials

questions.explanation: A link is a wired or wireless connection through which data travels between network nodes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network protocol?

options.A: A physical cable used to connect devices
options.B: A set of rules that governs communication and data exchange between devices
options.C: A device that amplifies network signals
options.D: A type of network topology

questions.explanation: A network protocol is a set of rules that governs communication and data exchange between devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the most widely used protocol suite on the Internet?

options.A: AppleTalk
options.B: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol)
options.C: IPX/SPX
options.D: NetBEUI

questions.explanation: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the most widely used protocol suite on the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network topology?

options.A: The speed of data transfer in a network
options.B: The physical or logical arrangement of devices and communication links in a network
options.C: The security policy applied to a network
options.D: The type of cable used in a network

questions.explanation: A network topology is the physical or logical arrangement of devices and communication links in a network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is bus topology?

options.A: A topology in which each device connects to a central device
options.B: A topology in which devices share a common main communication cable called a backbone
options.C: A topology in which devices are connected in a closed loop
options.D: A topology in which every device connects to every other device

questions.explanation: In bus topology, devices share a common main communication cable called a backbone.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is star topology?

options.A: A topology in which each device connects to a central device, commonly a switch or hub
options.B: A topology in which devices are connected in a closed loop
options.C: A topology in which devices share a single backbone cable
options.D: A topology that combines two or more different topology types

questions.explanation: In star topology, each device connects to a central device, commonly a switch or hub.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is ring topology?

options.A: A topology in which devices are connected in a closed loop, with each node linked to neighbouring nodes
options.B: A topology in which each device connects to a central hub
options.C: A topology in which devices share a common backbone cable
options.D: A hierarchical topology connecting groups of star networks

questions.explanation: In ring topology, devices are connected in a closed loop, with each node linked to neighbouring nodes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is mesh topology?

options.A: A topology in which devices are interconnected through multiple links, providing alternative paths for data
options.B: A topology in which all devices connect to a single central switch
options.C: A topology in which devices share one common cable
options.D: A topology in which devices are arranged in a closed loop

questions.explanation: In mesh topology, devices are interconnected through multiple links, providing alternative paths for data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is tree topology?

options.A: A topology in which devices are connected in a single closed loop
options.B: A hierarchical topology that connects groups of star networks or devices through a branching structure
options.C: A topology in which every device connects directly to every other device
options.D: A topology in which all devices share a common backbone cable

questions.explanation: Tree topology is a hierarchical topology that connects groups of star networks or devices through a branching structure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hybrid topology?

options.A: A topology that uses only wireless links
options.B: A network design that combines two or more different topology types
options.C: A topology in which all devices connect to a central hub
options.D: A topology used only in WANs

questions.explanation: A hybrid topology is a network design that combines two or more different topology types.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which topology commonly uses a central switch in an office LAN?

options.A: Bus topology
options.B: Ring topology
options.C: Star topology
options.D: Mesh topology

questions.explanation: Star topology commonly uses a central switch in an office LAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a wired network?

options.A: A network in which devices communicate using radio waves
options.B: A network in which devices communicate through physical media such as copper Ethernet cables or fibre-optic cables
options.C: A network that uses only satellite links
options.D: A network that does not require any hardware

questions.explanation: A wired network is one in which devices communicate through physical media such as copper Ethernet cables or fibre-optic cables.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a wireless network?

options.A: A network in which devices communicate using radio waves or other wireless transmission methods rather than a direct data cable
options.B: A network that uses only fibre-optic cables
options.C: A network that requires physical cables for every device
options.D: A network that cannot share resources

questions.explanation: A wireless network is one in which devices communicate using radio waves or other wireless transmission methods rather than a direct data cable.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network medium?

options.A: A software program that manages network traffic
options.B: The physical or wireless channel through which network signals are transmitted
options.C: A type of network protocol
options.D: A device that connects two networks

questions.explanation: A network medium is the physical or wireless channel through which network signals are transmitted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are common wired network media?

options.A: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
options.B: Twisted-pair copper cable, coaxial cable and optical fibre
options.C: Infrared and microwave
options.D: Satellite and cellular radio

questions.explanation: Common wired network media include twisted-pair copper cable, coaxial cable and optical fibre.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Ethernet?

options.A: A wireless networking standard based on IEEE 802.11
options.B: A widely used family of wired local area networking technologies standardised as IEEE 802.3
options.C: A protocol used only for satellite communication
options.D: A type of IP address

questions.explanation: Ethernet is a widely used family of wired local area networking technologies standardised as IEEE 802.3.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a MAC address?

options.A: A logical address used for routing between networks
options.B: A link-layer address used to identify a network interface on a local network; common Ethernet MAC addresses are 48 bits long
options.C: A 128-bit address used by IPv6
options.D: A name used to identify a Wi-Fi network

questions.explanation: A MAC address is a link-layer address used to identify a network interface on a local network; common Ethernet MAC addresses are 48 bits long.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an IP address?

options.A: A physical address burned into a network card
options.B: A logical address used by the Internet Protocol to identify an interface and support packet delivery across networks
options.C: A name used to identify a Wi-Fi network
options.D: A port number used by TCP

questions.explanation: An IP address is a logical address used by the Internet Protocol to identify an interface and support packet delivery across networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a MAC address and an IP address?

options.A: A MAC address is used for logical routing; an IP address is used for local delivery
options.B: A MAC address is used for local link-layer delivery; an IP address is used for logical addressing and routing between networks
options.C: Both are used only for local delivery
options.D: A MAC address is 128 bits long; an IP address is 48 bits long

questions.explanation: A MAC address is used for local link-layer delivery; an IP address is used for logical addressing and routing between networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a packet in networking?

options.A: A physical cable used in Ethernet networks
options.B: A formatted unit of data carried by a network protocol
options.C: A device that connects multiple networks
options.D: A type of network topology

questions.explanation: A packet is a formatted unit of data carried by a network protocol.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is packet switching?

options.A: A method in which a dedicated physical circuit is established for each communication session
options.B: A communication method in which data is divided into packets that are forwarded through a network and reassembled or processed at the destination
options.C: A method of encrypting all network traffic
options.D: A technique for assigning IP addresses automatically

questions.explanation: Packet switching is a communication method in which data is divided into packets that are forwarded through a network and reassembled or processed at the destination.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is bandwidth?

options.A: The actual rate at which data is successfully transferred
options.B: The maximum data-carrying capacity of a network connection, commonly expressed in bits per second
options.C: The delay experienced by data travelling through a network
options.D: The variation in packet delay over time

questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum data-carrying capacity of a network connection, commonly expressed in bits per second.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is throughput?

options.A: The maximum theoretical capacity of a link
options.B: The actual rate at which data is successfully transferred over a network
options.C: The delay experienced by data travelling through a network
options.D: The number of packets lost during transmission

questions.explanation: Throughput is the actual rate at which data is successfully transferred over a network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is latency?

options.A: The maximum data-carrying capacity of a connection
options.B: The delay experienced by data travelling through a network, commonly measured in milliseconds
options.C: The variation in packet delay over time
options.D: The failure of packets to reach their destination

questions.explanation: Latency is the delay experienced by data travelling through a network, commonly measured in milliseconds.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is jitter?

options.A: The total amount of data transferred in a second
options.B: Variation in packet delay over time, which can affect real-time audio and video communication
options.C: The maximum capacity of a wireless channel
options.D: The physical distance between two network nodes

questions.explanation: Jitter is variation in packet delay over time, which can affect real-time audio and video communication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is packet loss?

options.A: The failure of one or more transmitted packets to reach their destination
options.B: The maximum capacity of a network link
options.C: The delay experienced by data in a network
options.D: The variation in packet delay over time

questions.explanation: Packet loss is the failure of one or more transmitted packets to reach their destination.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is full-duplex communication?

options.A: Communication in which data travels in only one direction
options.B: Communication in which data can be transmitted and received simultaneously
options.C: Communication in which data can travel in both directions but not at the same time
options.D: Communication that uses only wireless media

questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication is communication in which data can be transmitted and received simultaneously.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is half-duplex communication?

options.A: Communication in which data travels in only one direction
options.B: Communication in which data can travel in both directions, but not at the same time
options.C: Communication in which data can be transmitted and received simultaneously
options.D: Communication that requires fibre-optic cables

questions.explanation: Half-duplex communication is communication in which data can travel in both directions, but not at the same time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is simplex communication?

options.A: Communication in which data travels in only one direction
options.B: Communication in which data can travel in both directions but not at the same time
options.C: Communication in which data can be transmitted and received simultaneously
options.D: Communication that uses multiple channels at once

questions.explanation: Simplex communication is communication in which data travels in only one direction.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a client in a network?

options.A: A device or software application that requests services or resources from another system
options.B: A computer that provides services to other devices
options.C: A device that connects two different networks
options.D: A cable used to connect devices in a LAN

questions.explanation: A client is a device or software application that requests services or resources from another system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a server?

options.A: A device that requests services from another system
options.B: A computer or software system that provides services, data or resources to clients
options.C: A device that only connects network cables
options.D: A type of network topology

questions.explanation: A server is a computer or software system that provides services, data or resources to clients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is peer-to-peer networking?

options.A: A network model in which participating devices can share resources directly without relying entirely on a central server
options.B: A network model in which all devices depend on a central server
options.C: A network that uses only wireless connections
options.D: A network limited to a single building

questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer networking is a network model in which participating devices can share resources directly without relying entirely on a central server.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is client-server networking?

options.A: A network model in which devices share resources directly without a central server
options.B: A network model in which client devices request services or resources from centralised or designated servers
options.C: A network that connects only two devices
options.D: A network that uses only peer-to-peer protocols

questions.explanation: Client-server networking is a network model in which client devices request services or resources from centralised or designated servers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is a PAN?

options.A: A Personal Area Network; a small network connecting personal devices around an individual, usually over a short distance
options.B: A Public Area Network covering a city
options.C: A Private Access Node used in WANs
options.D: A Protocol Area Network used for routing

questions.explanation: A PAN is a Personal Area Network; a small network connecting personal devices around an individual, usually over a short distance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the typical coverage area of a PAN?

options.A: A few metres around a person, although the exact range depends on the technology used
options.B: A city or metropolitan region
options.C: A country or continent
options.D: A building or campus

questions.explanation: The typical coverage area of a PAN is a few metres around a person, although the exact range depends on the technology used.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of PAN technologies?

options.A: Bluetooth, USB connections and some short-range wireless technologies
options.B: Fibre-optic WAN links
options.C: Metropolitan Ethernet rings
options.D: Satellite backhaul links

questions.explanation: Examples of PAN technologies include Bluetooth, USB connections and some short-range wireless technologies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a PAN?

options.A: A smartphone connected to wireless earbuds and a smartwatch using Bluetooth
options.B: A city-wide network connecting government offices
options.C: A bank's private network connecting branches in different cities
options.D: A school computer laboratory network

questions.explanation: A smartphone connected to wireless earbuds and a smartwatch using Bluetooth is an example of a PAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is a LAN?

options.A: A Local Area Network; a network that connects devices within a limited geographical area such as a home, office, school or building
options.B: A Long Area Network covering countries
options.C: A Logical Access Node used in WANs
options.D: A network that connects only personal devices over a few metres

questions.explanation: A LAN is a Local Area Network; a network that connects devices within a limited geographical area such as a home, office, school or building.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the typical coverage area of a LAN?

options.A: A few metres around a person
options.B: A limited site or premises, such as a room, building or campus; there is no single fixed distance limit
options.C: A city or metropolitan area
options.D: A country or continent

questions.explanation: A LAN typically covers a limited site or premises, such as a room, building or campus; there is no single fixed distance limit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of LANs?

options.A: A home Wi-Fi network, a school computer laboratory network and an office Ethernet network
options.B: A smartphone connected to wireless earbuds
options.C: A bank's private network connecting branches in different cities
options.D: A global network of interconnected networks

questions.explanation: Examples of LANs include a home Wi-Fi network, a school computer laboratory network and an office Ethernet network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is a WLAN?

options.A: A Wide Local Area Network covering countries
options.B: A Wireless Local Area Network; a LAN that uses wireless communication, commonly Wi-Fi
options.C: A Wired Local Access Node
options.D: A network that connects only personal devices

questions.explanation: A WLAN is a Wireless Local Area Network; a LAN that uses wireless communication, commonly Wi-Fi.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Is every LAN wireless?

options.A: Yes, all LANs use Wi-Fi
options.B: No. A LAN may use wired Ethernet, wireless Wi-Fi or a combination of both
options.C: Yes, LANs cannot use cables
options.D: No, LANs can only use fibre-optic cables

questions.explanation: No. A LAN may use wired Ethernet, wireless Wi-Fi or a combination of both.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is a MAN?

options.A: A Metropolitan Area Network; a network that connects users or LANs across a city or metropolitan region
options.B: A Mobile Access Node used in PANs
options.C: A network that connects only personal devices
options.D: A global network of interconnected networks

questions.explanation: A MAN is a Metropolitan Area Network; a network that connects users or LANs across a city or metropolitan region.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the typical coverage area of a MAN?

options.A: A few metres around a person
options.B: A room or building
options.C: A city or metropolitan area; its exact size depends on the network design
options.D: A country or continent

questions.explanation: A MAN typically covers a city or metropolitan area; its exact size depends on the network design.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a MAN?

options.A: A smartphone connected to wireless earbuds using Bluetooth
options.B: A city-wide network connecting government offices, university buildings or multiple organisational sites
options.C: A home Wi-Fi network
options.D: The global Internet

questions.explanation: A city-wide network connecting government offices, university buildings or multiple organisational sites is an example of a MAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is a WAN?

options.A: A Wireless Access Node used in LANs
options.B: A Wide Area Network; a network that connects devices or smaller networks across large geographical areas, such as regions, countries or continents
options.C: A network limited to a single building
options.D: A network connecting personal devices over a few metres

questions.explanation: A WAN is a Wide Area Network; a network that connects devices or smaller networks across large geographical areas, such as regions, countries or continents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the largest and best-known example of a WAN?

options.A: A home Wi-Fi network
options.B: A school computer laboratory network
options.C: The Internet, which is a global network of interconnected networks
options.D: A Bluetooth connection between a phone and earbuds

questions.explanation: The Internet is the largest and best-known example of a WAN; it is a global network of interconnected networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a private WAN?

options.A: A smartphone connected to wireless earbuds
options.B: A bank's private network connecting branches in different cities
options.C: A home Wi-Fi network
options.D: A Bluetooth connection between a keyboard and a computer

questions.explanation: A bank's private network connecting branches in different cities is an example of a private WAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the difference between PAN and LAN?

options.A: PAN connects an individual's nearby personal devices; LAN connects devices within a home, office, building or similar local area
options.B: PAN covers a city; LAN covers a country
options.C: PAN is always wired; LAN is always wireless
options.D: PAN connects networks across continents; LAN connects personal devices

questions.explanation: PAN connects an individual's nearby personal devices; LAN connects devices within a home, office, building or similar local area.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the difference between LAN and MAN?

options.A: LAN covers a limited local site; MAN connects networks across a city or metropolitan area
options.B: LAN covers a country; MAN covers a building
options.C: LAN is always wireless; MAN is always wired
options.D: LAN connects personal devices; MAN connects only servers

questions.explanation: LAN covers a limited local site; MAN connects networks across a city or metropolitan area.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the difference between MAN and WAN?

options.A: MAN generally covers a metropolitan region; WAN spans much larger geographical areas, often across countries or continents
options.B: MAN spans continents; WAN covers a building
options.C: MAN connects personal devices; WAN connects only LANs in one room
options.D: MAN is always wireless; WAN is always wired

questions.explanation: MAN generally covers a metropolitan region; WAN spans much larger geographical areas, often across countries or continents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which network type generally has the smallest coverage area among PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN?

options.A: PAN
options.B: LAN
options.C: MAN
options.D: WAN

questions.explanation: PAN generally has the smallest coverage area among PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which network type connects devices within a building or office?

options.A: PAN
options.B: LAN
options.C: MAN
options.D: WAN

questions.explanation: LAN connects devices within a building or office.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which network type is designed to cover a city?

options.A: PAN
options.B: LAN
options.C: MAN
options.D: WAN

questions.explanation: MAN is designed to cover a city or metropolitan area.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Which network type connects networks over countries or continents?

options.A: PAN
options.B: LAN
options.C: MAN
options.D: WAN

questions.explanation: WAN connects networks over countries or continents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Arrange PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN in increasing geographical coverage.

options.A: PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN
options.B: WAN, MAN, LAN, PAN
options.C: LAN, PAN, WAN, MAN
options.D: MAN, LAN, PAN, WAN

questions.explanation: In increasing geographical coverage: PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: Does a WAN always use the public Internet?

options.A: Yes, all WANs use the public Internet
options.B: No. A WAN may use private leased links, carrier networks, VPNs or a combination of technologies
options.C: Yes, WANs cannot use private links
options.D: No, WANs can only use Bluetooth

questions.explanation: No. A WAN may use private leased links, carrier networks, VPNs or a combination of technologies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is an intranet?

options.A: A global public network of networks
options.B: A private organisational network that uses Internet technologies and is accessible only to authorised users
options.C: A network that connects only personal devices
options.D: A city-wide network

questions.explanation: An intranet is a private organisational network that uses Internet technologies and is accessible only to authorised users.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is an extranet?

options.A: A controlled extension of an organisation's intranet that gives authorised external users, such as suppliers or partners, access to selected resources
options.B: A global public network of networks
options.C: A network limited to a single room
options.D: A network that connects only personal devices

questions.explanation: An extranet is a controlled extension of an organisation's intranet that gives authorised external users, such as suppliers or partners, access to selected resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is the difference between the Internet and an intranet?

options.A: The Internet is a global public network of networks; an intranet is a private network restricted to an organisation or authorised users
options.B: The Internet is private; an intranet is public
options.C: Both are restricted to a single organisation
options.D: Both are global public networks

questions.explanation: The Internet is a global public network of networks; an intranet is a private network restricted to an organisation or authorised users.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Types of Networks: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
questions.question: What is a campus area network (CAN)?

options.A: A network that connects LANs across a university, business campus or similar group of nearby buildings
options.B: A network that spans countries or continents
options.C: A network that connects only personal devices over a few metres
options.D: A network that connects a single computer to a printer

questions.explanation: A campus area network (CAN) is a network that connects LANs across a university, business campus or similar group of nearby buildings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network device?

options.A: A software program used to create documents
options.B: Hardware used to connect devices, forward data, control network traffic or provide network access and services
options.C: A type of network topology
options.D: A protocol used for encrypting data

questions.explanation: A network device is hardware used to connect devices, forward data, control network traffic or provide network access and services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are common network devices?

options.A: Network interface card, hub, switch, router, modem, wireless access point, repeater, bridge, gateway and firewall
options.B: Keyboard, mouse, monitor and printer
options.C: CPU, RAM, hard disk and motherboard
options.D: Operating system, compiler and interpreter

questions.explanation: Common network devices include network interface card, hub, switch, router, modem, wireless access point, repeater, bridge, gateway and firewall.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Network Interface Card (NIC)?

options.A: A hardware component that enables a computer or other device to connect to a network
options.B: A device that connects two different IP networks
options.C: A device that regenerates network signals
options.D: A software firewall

questions.explanation: A Network Interface Card (NIC) is a hardware component that enables a computer or other device to connect to a network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is another name for a NIC?

options.A: Network adapter or network interface controller
options.B: Router or gateway
options.C: Hub or repeater
options.D: Modem or ONT

questions.explanation: A NIC is also called a network adapter or network interface controller.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an Ethernet NIC?

options.A: A network interface that connects a device to a wireless network
options.B: A network interface that connects a device to a wired Ethernet network
options.C: A device that connects two IP networks
options.D: A device that converts signals for DSL

questions.explanation: An Ethernet NIC is a network interface that connects a device to a wired Ethernet network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a wireless network adapter?

options.A: A network interface that allows a device to connect to a wireless network, commonly Wi-Fi
options.B: A device that connects two IP networks
options.C: A device that regenerates signals to extend distance

questions.explanation: A wireless network adapter is a network interface that allows a device to connect to a wireless network, commonly Wi-Fi.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hub?

options.A: A basic network device that connects multiple Ethernet devices and repeats incoming data to all other ports
options.B: A device that forwards frames using MAC addresses
options.C: A device that forwards IP packets between networks
options.D: A device that converts signals for Internet access

questions.explanation: A hub is a basic network device that connects multiple Ethernet devices and repeats incoming data to all other ports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: At which OSI layer does a traditional Ethernet hub operate?

options.A: Physical layer (Layer 1)
options.B: Data Link layer (Layer 2)
options.C: Network layer (Layer 3)
options.D: Transport layer (Layer 4)

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a disadvantage of a traditional hub?

options.A: It sends incoming signals to all other ports, creating unnecessary traffic and sharing bandwidth
options.B: It forwards frames only to the destination port
options.C: It requires configuration of MAC address tables
options.D: It operates at the Network layer

questions.explanation: A disadvantage of a traditional hub is that it sends incoming signals to all other ports, creating unnecessary traffic and sharing bandwidth.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a switch?

options.A: A device that repeats signals to all ports
options.B: A network device that connects devices in a LAN and forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses
options.C: A device that forwards IP packets between networks
options.D: A device that modulates and demodulates signals

questions.explanation: A switch is a network device that connects devices in a LAN and forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: At which OSI layer does a basic Ethernet switch operate?

options.A: Physical layer (Layer 1)
options.B: Data Link layer (Layer 2)
options.C: Network layer (Layer 3)
options.D: Application layer (Layer 7)

questions.explanation: A basic Ethernet switch operates at the Data Link layer (Layer 2).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does a basic Ethernet switch learn where to forward frames?

options.A: It learns source MAC addresses and associates them with the ports on which they are received
options.B: It uses a routing table of IP addresses
options.C: It broadcasts every frame to all ports permanently
options.D: It relies on a DNS server

questions.explanation: A basic Ethernet switch learns source MAC addresses and associates them with the ports on which they are received.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a switch MAC address table?

options.A: A table that maps learned MAC addresses to switch ports for frame forwarding
options.B: A table that maps IP addresses to domain names
options.C: A table that stores routing paths between networks
options.D: A table that lists Wi-Fi network names

questions.explanation: A switch MAC address table maps learned MAC addresses to switch ports for frame forwarding.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens when a switch receives a frame for a known destination MAC address?

options.B: It floods the frame to all ports
options.C: It discards the frame
options.D: It sends the frame to the default gateway

questions.explanation: When a switch receives a frame for a known destination MAC address, it normally forwards the frame only through the port associated with that destination, subject to VLAN and filtering rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens when a switch receives a frame with an unknown destination MAC address?

options.A: It generally floods the frame to relevant ports in the same VLAN, except the incoming port

options.D: It sends the frame back to the source port

questions.explanation: When a switch receives a frame with an unknown destination MAC address, it generally floods the frame to relevant ports in the same VLAN, except the incoming port.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a router?

options.A: A network-layer device that connects different IP networks and forwards packets between them using routing information
options.B: A device that repeats signals to all ports

questions.explanation: A router is a network-layer device that connects different IP networks and forwards packets between them using routing information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main function of a router?

options.B: To repeat signals to all ports

questions.explanation: The main function of a router is to select a path and forward IP packets between different networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a modem?

options.A: A modulator-demodulator; a device that converts signals so digital data can be transmitted over a particular communication medium or access network
options.B: A device that forwards frames using MAC addresses
options.C: A device that connects two IP networks
options.D: A device that regenerates signals to extend distance

questions.explanation: A modem is a modulator-demodulator; a device that converts signals so digital data can be transmitted over a particular communication medium or access network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a wireless access point (AP)?

options.B: A device that forwards IP packets between networks
options.C: A device that converts signals for DSL
options.D: A device that stores files for network users

questions.explanation: A wireless access point (AP) is a device that allows Wi-Fi clients to connect to a wired local area network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a repeater?

options.A: A device that regenerates or retransmits a signal to extend the distance over which it can travel

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a basic repeater operate?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a bridge in networking?

options.A: A device that connects network segments and forwards frames based on MAC addresses
options.B: A device that forwards IP packets between networks

questions.question: At which OSI layer does a traditional bridge operate?

options.A: Physical layer (Layer 1)
options.B: Data Link layer (Layer 2)

options.D: Transport layer (Layer 4)

questions.explanation: A traditional bridge operates at the Data Link layer (Layer 2).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a gateway?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a default gateway?

options.C: A device that regenerates signals to extend distance
options.D: A device that distributes incoming requests across servers

questions.explanation: A default gateway is the router or other next-hop device to which a host sends traffic destined for networks outside its local subnet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a firewall?

options.A: A hardware or software security system that monitors and controls network traffic according to defined rules
options.B: A device that connects network segments and forwards frames
options.C: A device that converts signals for Internet access
options.D: A device that distributes requests across servers

questions.explanation: A firewall is a hardware or software security system that monitors and controls network traffic according to defined rules.

questions.question: What is a network firewall used for?

options.B: To assign IP addresses to network devices

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a load balancer?

options.A: A device or software service that distributes incoming network requests across multiple servers or resources
options.B: A device that connects two IP networks

options.D: A device that regenerates signals to extend distance

questions.explanation: A load balancer is a device or software service that distributes incoming network requests across multiple servers or resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network-attached storage (NAS) device?

options.C: A device that connects networks using different protocols

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Power over Ethernet (PoE) switch?

questions.question: What information does a router use to forward IP packets?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.question: What is a router's WAN or Internet port used for?

options.A: The loopback address 127.0.0.1, used by a device to communicate with itself
options.B: The default gateway address
options.C: The broadcast address
options.D: The DNS server address

questions.explanation: In IPv4, localhost is the loopback address 127.0.0.1, used by a device to communicate with itself.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the IPv6 loopback address?
questions.explanation: The IPv6 loopback address is ::1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a subnet mask?

options.A: A value used with an IPv4 address to identify the network portion and host portion of the address
options.B: A value used to encrypt network traffic
options.C: A value used to assign IP addresses automatically
options.D: A value used to resolve domain names

questions.explanation: A subnet mask is a value used with an IPv4 address to identify the network portion and host portion of the address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a subnet?

options.A: A logically divided portion of an IP network
options.B: A type of network topology
options.C: A device that connects two IP networks
options.D: A protocol used for network control and diagnostic messages

questions.explanation: A subnet is a logically divided portion of an IP network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a default gateway in a computer's network settings?

options.A: The next-hop router used to reach destinations outside the local subnet
options.B: The DNS server address
options.C: The loopback address
options.D: The broadcast address

questions.explanation: A default gateway in a computer's network settings is the next-hop router used to reach destinations outside the local subnet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is DNS?

options.A: The Domain Name System, which translates domain names into IP addresses and provides other naming data
options.B: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol, which automatically supplies IP configuration to network clients
options.C: Address Resolution Protocol, used to discover link-layer addresses
options.D: Internet Control Message Protocol, used for network control and diagnostic messages

questions.explanation: DNS is the Domain Name System, which translates domain names into IP addresses and provides other naming data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is DHCP?

options.A: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol, which automatically supplies IP configuration to network clients
options.B: The Domain Name System, which translates domain names into IP addresses
options.C: Address Resolution Protocol, used to discover link-layer addresses
options.D: Internet Control Message Protocol, used for network control and diagnostic messages

questions.explanation: DHCP is Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol, which automatically supplies IP configuration to network clients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is ARP?

options.A: Address Resolution Protocol, used on IPv4 local networks to discover the link-layer address associated with an IPv4 address
options.B: A protocol that translates domain names into IP addresses
options.C: A protocol that automatically supplies IP configuration to network clients
options.D: A protocol used for network control and diagnostic messages

questions.explanation: ARP is Address Resolution Protocol, used on IPv4 local networks to discover the link-layer address associated with an IPv4 address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is ICMP?

options.A: Internet Control Message Protocol, used for network control and diagnostic messages; tools such as ping commonly use it
options.B: A protocol that translates domain names into IP addresses
options.C: A protocol that automatically supplies IP configuration to network clients
options.D: A protocol used to discover link-layer addresses

questions.explanation: ICMP is Internet Control Message Protocol, used for network control and diagnostic messages; tools such as ping commonly use it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is ping?

options.A: A network diagnostic utility that commonly uses ICMP Echo messages to test reachability and measure round-trip time
options.B: A utility that resolves domain names into IP addresses
options.C: A utility that automatically supplies IP configuration
options.D: A utility that discovers link-layer addresses

questions.explanation: Ping is a network diagnostic utility that commonly uses ICMP Echo messages to test reachability and measure round-trip time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is traceroute or tracert?

options.A: A diagnostic utility that attempts to show the sequence of routers or hops a packet takes toward a destination
options.B: A utility that resolves domain names into IP addresses
options.C: A utility that automatically supplies IP configuration
options.D: A utility that discovers link-layer addresses

questions.explanation: Traceroute or tracert is a diagnostic utility that attempts to show the sequence of routers or hops a packet takes toward a destination.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a VPN?

options.A: A Virtual Private Network creates a protected logical connection over another network, commonly using encryption and authentication
options.B: A Very Private Node used in WANs
options.C: A Virtual Public Network that is always unencrypted
options.D: A type of network topology

questions.explanation: A VPN is a Virtual Private Network; it creates a protected logical connection over another network, commonly using encryption and authentication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is network encryption?

options.A: The use of cryptographic methods to protect data transmitted over a network from unauthorised reading
options.B: The process of verifying the identity of a user or device
options.C: The process of assigning IP addresses
options.D: The process of resolving domain names

questions.explanation: Network encryption is the use of cryptographic methods to protect data transmitted over a network from unauthorised reading.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is network authentication?

options.A: The process of verifying the identity of a user or device before granting network access
options.B: The use of cryptographic methods to protect transmitted data
options.C: The process of assigning IP addresses
options.D: The process of resolving domain names

questions.explanation: Network authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user or device before granting network access.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is network access control?

options.A: A set of policies and technologies used to control which users and devices may connect to network resources
options.B: The use of cryptographic methods to protect transmitted data
options.C: The process of assigning IP addresses
options.D: The process of resolving domain names

questions.explanation: Network access control is a set of policies and technologies used to control which users and devices may connect to network resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a denial-of-service (DoS) attack?

options.A: An attack intended to make a system or network service unavailable by overwhelming or disrupting it
options.B: An attack that steals user credentials
options.C: An attack that encrypts files and demands payment
options.D: An attack that intercepts network traffic

questions.explanation: A denial-of-service (DoS) attack is an attack intended to make a system or network service unavailable by overwhelming or disrupting it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack?

options.A: A DoS attack launched from multiple systems or sources, often a botnet
options.B: A DoS attack launched from a single system
options.C: An attack that steals user credentials
options.D: An attack that encrypts files and demands payment

questions.explanation: A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack is a DoS attack launched from multiple systems or sources, often a botnet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a packet-filtering firewall?

options.A: A firewall that allows or blocks network packets based on rules such as source/destination addresses, protocols and ports
options.B: A firewall that only inspects application content
options.C: A firewall that only encrypts network traffic
options.D: A firewall that only assigns IP addresses

questions.explanation: A packet-filtering firewall allows or blocks network packets based on rules such as source/destination addresses, protocols and ports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is network monitoring?

options.A: The observation and analysis of network availability, performance, traffic and security events
options.B: The process of assigning IP addresses
options.C: The process of resolving domain names
options.D: The process of encrypting network traffic

questions.explanation: Network monitoring is the observation and analysis of network availability, performance, traffic and security events.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an Ethernet cable?

options.A: A cable used to connect devices in wired Ethernet networks, commonly using twisted-pair copper and RJ45-style connectors
options.B: A cable that carries data as pulses of light
options.C: A cable used only for satellite communication
options.D: A cable used only for Bluetooth connections

questions.explanation: An Ethernet cable is a cable used to connect devices in wired Ethernet networks, commonly using twisted-pair copper and RJ45-style connectors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an RJ45 connector commonly used for?

options.A: Connecting twisted-pair Ethernet cables to network devices; the common modular connector is technically an 8P8C connector
options.B: Connecting fibre-optic cables to network devices
options.C: Connecting Bluetooth devices
options.D: Connecting satellite dishes

questions.explanation: An RJ45 connector is commonly used for connecting twisted-pair Ethernet cables to network devices; the common modular connector is technically an 8P8C connector.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an optical fibre cable?

options.A: A cable that carries data as pulses of light through glass or plastic fibres
options.B: A cable that carries data as electrical signals through copper wires
options.C: A cable used only for Bluetooth connections
options.D: A cable used only for satellite communication

questions.explanation: An optical fibre cable is a cable that carries data as pulses of light through glass or plastic fibres.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main advantage of fibre-optic communication?

options.A: It supports high bandwidth over long distances and is resistant to electromagnetic interference
options.B: It is the cheapest cable type available
options.C: It is easier to install than copper cable
options.D: It can only be used for short distances

questions.explanation: The main advantage of fibre-optic communication is that it supports high bandwidth over long distances and is resistant to electromagnetic interference.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the IEEE 802.3 standard associated with?

options.A: Ethernet wired networking
options.B: Wireless LAN technologies commonly known as Wi-Fi
options.C: Bluetooth
options.D: Cellular mobile networks

questions.explanation: The IEEE 802.3 standard is associated with Ethernet wired networking.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the IEEE 802.11 standard associated with?

options.A: Wireless LAN technologies commonly known as Wi-Fi
options.B: Ethernet wired networking
options.C: Bluetooth
options.D: Cellular mobile networks

questions.explanation: The IEEE 802.11 standard is associated with wireless LAN technologies commonly known as Wi-Fi.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the IEEE 802.15.1 standard historically associated with?

options.A: Bluetooth; Bluetooth specifications are now maintained by the Bluetooth SIG rather than being developed as an active IEEE 802.15.1 standard
options.B: Ethernet wired networking
options.C: Wi-Fi wireless LAN
options.D: Cellular mobile networks

questions.explanation: The IEEE 802.15.1 standard is historically associated with Bluetooth; Bluetooth specifications are now maintained by the Bluetooth SIG rather than being developed as an active IEEE 802.15.1 standard.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between LAN and WAN.

options.A: LAN covers a limited local area such as a building; WAN connects networks over large geographical areas
options.B: LAN connects networks over countries; WAN covers a building
options.C: LAN is always wireless; WAN is always wired
options.D: LAN and WAN are exactly the same

questions.explanation: LAN covers a limited local area such as a building; WAN connects networks over large geographical areas.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between PAN and WLAN.

options.A: PAN connects an individual's nearby personal devices; WLAN is a wireless local area network serving a local site
options.B: PAN covers a city; WLAN covers a country
options.C: PAN is always wired; WLAN is always wired
options.D: PAN and WLAN are exactly the same

questions.explanation: PAN connects an individual's nearby personal devices; WLAN is a wireless local area network serving a local site.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between a hub and a switch.

options.A: A hub repeats signals to all ports; a switch forwards frames based on learned MAC addresses
options.B: A hub forwards frames based on MAC addresses; a switch repeats signals to all ports
options.C: A hub operates at Layer 3; a switch operates at Layer 1
options.D: A hub and a switch are exactly the same

questions.explanation: A hub repeats signals to all ports; a switch forwards frames based on learned MAC addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between a switch and a router.

options.A: A switch connects devices within a LAN and forwards frames; a router connects IP networks and forwards packets
options.B: A switch connects IP networks and forwards packets; a router connects devices within a LAN and forwards frames
options.C: A switch operates at Layer 3; a router operates at Layer 2
options.D: A switch and a router are exactly the same

questions.explanation: A switch connects devices within a LAN and forwards frames; a router connects IP networks and forwards packets.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between a modem and a router.

options.A: A modem or access device connects to the ISP's access network; a router directs traffic between networks
options.B: A modem directs traffic between networks; a router connects to the ISP's access network
options.C: A modem and a router are exactly the same
options.D: A modem operates at Layer 3; a router operates at Layer 1

questions.explanation: A modem or access device connects to the ISP's access network; a router directs traffic between networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between an access point and a router.

options.A: An access point provides wireless access to a LAN; a router forwards traffic between networks. A home device may combine both functions
options.B: An access point forwards traffic between networks; a router provides wireless access to a LAN
options.C: An access point and a router are exactly the same
options.D: An access point operates at Layer 3; a router operates at Layer 1

questions.explanation: An access point provides wireless access to a LAN; a router forwards traffic between networks. A home device may combine both functions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

options.A: Wi-Fi is mainly used for wireless LAN connectivity; Bluetooth is mainly used for short-range personal device connections
options.B: Wi-Fi is mainly used for short-range personal device connections; Bluetooth is mainly used for wireless LAN connectivity
options.C: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are exactly the same
options.D: Wi-Fi operates only in the 2.4 GHz band; Bluetooth operates only in the 5 GHz band

questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is mainly used for wireless LAN connectivity; Bluetooth is mainly used for short-range personal device connections.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate between wired and wireless networks.

options.A: Wired networks use physical cabling; wireless networks use radio or other wireless signals
options.B: Wired networks use radio signals; wireless networks use physical cabling
options.C: Wired and wireless networks are exactly the same
options.D: Wired networks cannot share resources

questions.explanation: Wired networks use physical cabling; wireless networks use radio or other wireless signals.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which network type is suitable for connecting a person's phone, watch and earbuds?

options.A: PAN
options.B: LAN
options.C: MAN
options.D: WAN

questions.explanation: A PAN is suitable for connecting a person's phone, watch and earbuds.

questions.question: Which network type is suitable for connecting computers in a school laboratory?

options.A: LAN
options.B: PAN
options.C: MAN
options.D: WAN

questions.explanation: A LAN is suitable for connecting computers in a school laboratory.

questions.question: Which network type can connect branches across several countries?

options.A: WAN
options.B: PAN
options.C: LAN
options.D: MAN

options.B: PAN
options.C: LAN
options.D: WAN

questions.question: Which device forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses?

options.B: A router

options.D: A modem

questions.question: Which device forwards IP packets between networks?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device repeats incoming Ethernet signals to all ports?

options.A: A traditional hub
options.B: A router
options.C: A switch
options.D: A modem

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device provides wireless access to a wired LAN?

options.A: A wireless access point
options.B: A router
options.C: A hub
options.D: A modem

questions.explanation: A wireless access point provides wireless access to a wired LAN.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device regenerates a signal to extend its reach?

options.A: A repeater
options.B: A router
options.C: A switch
options.D: A modem

questions.question: Which device modulates and demodulates signals for a communication link?

options.A: A modem
options.B: A router
options.C: A switch
options.D: A repeater

questions.explanation: A modem modulates and demodulates signals for a communication link.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which device provides a network interface to a computer?

options.A: A NIC or network adapter
options.B: A router
options.C: A switch
options.D: A modem

questions.explanation: A NIC or network adapter provides a network interface to a computer.

questions.question: Which technology is commonly used for wireless LANs?

options.A: Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11)

options.D: DSL

questions.question: Which technology is commonly used for short-range connections between headphones and phones?

options.A: Bluetooth

options.D: DSL

options.D: No security is needed

questions.question: What is the common Bluetooth operating frequency band?

options.D: Yes, but only for audio devices

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the usual purpose of a default gateway?

options.A: To forward traffic from a local network to destinations outside that network

options.D: To encrypt wireless traffic

questions.explanation: The usual purpose of a default gateway is to forward traffic from a local network to destinations outside that network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the safest basic practice for a home Wi-Fi router?

options.A: Use WPA2-AES or WPA3, set a strong unique Wi-Fi password, change default administrator credentials and install firmware updates
